data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 asserts the decentralized network is 'actually more fragile' than a monolith once shared low-level dependencies create a 'shadow monolith,' but this only compares correlated-failure *likelihood* and ignores the monolith's own correlated-failure surface. A monolith with strictly more total internal redundancy still propagates single logic bugs or bad-config-pushes across all its redundant internal components, so even in the shared-dependency worst case the decentralized network is not *more* fragile—it has a different (and not strictly worse) correlated-failure profile. The argument needs a head-to-head showing that the decentralized shared-dependency trigger causes strictly more total correlated failures than the monolith's own design-level monopathia.
